summary: Iter43 backlog tested (b=save-drop+per-maker-tag, c=cohort retention, d=community_chat refactor + WS flows). Backend pytest 23/24 PASSING in /app/backend/tests/test_iter43_save_drop_cohorts_chat.py. The 1 failure exposes a CRITICAL functional bug in kit_service.create_drop_broadcast_targeted: Kit's V4 API silently rejects the subscriber_filter shape `[{type:'tag', any:[<tag_id>]}]` we send and falls back to `all_subscribers`, so every high-value drop (>=$250) is currently being broadcast to the ENTIRE newsletter list — defeating the per-maker tag-targeting feature. Test fetches /v4/broadcasts/{id} after creation and asserts on the saved subscriber_filter structure (then deletes the broadcast). All other backend coverage green: save-drop creates Kit subscriber+tag (idempotent same tag_id on repeat), persists to db.drop_saves, /api/admin/drop-saves listing+filter+auth gate; cohort endpoint returns 12-week heatmap with weeks clamped to 4..26; chat REST history+buddies+unknown channel; WS unauth=4401, valid buyer connects, makers-only rejects buyer, live_chat_enabled=false closes 4503, per-channel mute returns private system notice; forum + showcase unaffected by community.py slim. Frontend Playwright PASSING: SaveDropButton on ProductDetail (mountain-range-silhouette) — empty heart → click opens inline form → submit → toast/SAVED + heart fills with class fill-[#ff4500] → reload preserves filled heart via localStorage. Admin Retention tab present between Analytics and Web Analytics, 3 stat cards (Total Buyers/Repeat Buyers/Repeat %) render, retention-grid heatmap renders, weeks selector switches across 8 / 26.

critical.issue: subscriber_filter `[{type:'tag', any:[int_tag_id]}]` is silently rejected by Kit V4 — fetched broadcast comes back with subscriber_filter=[{any:[{type:'all_subscribers'}]}]. So per-maker tag targeting is NOT being applied — every high-value publish currently emails the WHOLE newsletter, not just `interested-in-{slug}`. Likely correct shape per Kit (undocumented): `[{any:[{type:'tag', tag_id:<int>}]}]` (type lives INSIDE the any[] array). Worth confirming with Kit support, but the all_subscribers default observed in the response is the smoking gun.

Both return HTTP 500 with ResponseValidationError: product `topo-mountains` has no `description` field in Mongo, but the FastAPI response model marks `description` as required. Side-effects: (a) ProductDetail `/shop/topo-mountains` page is unloadable, (b) the entire /shop listing 500s because at least one product fails validation. Fix: either backfill `description` on the seed doc or make the field Optional in the response model.

URGENT — restore Shop and topo-mountains. Either UPDATE products SET description='<seed text>' on slug='topo-mountains' or change the product response model to make description Optional[str] = None. /api/shop is fully broken until then.
Optional polish — admin/drop-saves UI tab to surface saved-drop emails in the dashboard so admins can see the targeting audience (the API exists already).
critical_code_review_comments: kit_service.py: the saved-drop broadcast path swallows EVERY exception silently (logger.warning then return None). Combined with the subscriber_filter being rejected by Kit, there is currently NO observable signal that high-value drops are mis-targeted. Add a stronger log line when subscriber_filter is dropped or a returns assertion-style check.

kit_service.create_drop_broadcast_targeted: when tag_id resolution fails (_ensure_tag returns None), the code currently sends the broadcast WITHOUT subscriber_filter — i.e., to everyone. That's a fail-open security/marketing default that should at minimum be feature-flagged behind something like KIT_DROP_FALLBACK_ALL_SUBSCRIBERS=false.

routers/community_chat.py L177-199: per-channel mute lookup on every received message is an extra Mongo round-trip per chat message. Consider an in-memory TTL cache keyed by (user_email, channel) refreshed every ~60s, or eagerly load mutes at WS-connect time and refresh on admin-mute events.

routers/admin.py admin_cohorts: O(buyers * txs) loop with two _iso_to_week_key calls per tx is fine at current scale but will degrade when paid_orders > a few thousand — bucket once into a {week_key: [emails]} dict on first pass instead of recomputing per cohort.

newsletter.py /save-drop: HTTPException(502) wraps EVERY exception with the raw exception string truncated to 200 chars — ok for ops, but consider mapping Kit-specific errors (rate limit, auth) to 429/503 so the frontend can react differently.

topo-mountains seeding code path needs auditing — whatever created it (iter42 testing) bypassed the description-required validator. Either add a Mongo schema validator or make the response model match reality.

rca of the issue: Kit subscriber_filter mis-shape: looking at the saved broadcast structure `[{any:[{type:'all_subscribers'}]}]`, Kit V4 expects `type` to live INSIDE the any[] clause, not as a sibling key. Our payload `[{type:'tag', any:[<tag_id>]}]` therefore has no recognized type at the outer level → Kit treats it as 'no filter' and substitutes the default all_subscribers clause when persisting. Reproduction: pytest TestKitTargetedBroadcast::test_targeted_broadcast_uses_tag_filter — fails with the asserted `tag-type filter missing: [{'any': [{'type': 'all_subscribers'}]}]` message (the test deletes the broadcast on teardown so no live spam). Mitigation: change subscriber_filter to `[{'any': [{'type':'tag', 'tag_id': int(tag_id)}]}]` (most likely shape per Kit's other public API examples) and re-run the test until the response contains `type:'tag'`. Topo-mountains 500: a product was inserted in iter42 testing without `description` while the response Pydantic model requires it; the `/shop` list endpoint serializes the whole product set so a single bad row poisons the entire response. Either add the missing field or relax the model.
